title: Article 301 — Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse

content.overview: Article 301 provides that subject to the other provisions of Part XIII, trade, commerce and intercourse throughout the territory of India shall be free.
content.glance: Trade, commerce and intercourse throughout India shall be free, subject to Part XIII (Arts 302–305 restrictions).
content.study:
Article 301 is the general guarantee of free trade, commerce and intercourse throughout India:
- Covers trade, commerce and intercourse.
- Throughout the territory of India (inter-State and, subject to interpretation, aspects of intra-State trade affecting free flow).
- Subject to Part XIII — Articles 302–305 allow Parliament and States to impose restrictions in specified circumstances.
- Not an absolute freedom; regulatory measures that do not amount to a restriction on the freedom of trade as such may be sustained; fiscal and regulatory distinctions are developed in case law.

Examination: general freedom; subject to Part XIII; inter-State emphasis; link Arts 302–304.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: Subject to the other provisions of Part XIII, trade, commerce and intercourse throughout the territory of India shall be free.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does Article 301 provide?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 301 provides that subject to the other provisions of Part XIII, trade, commerce and intercourse throughout the territory of India shall be free. Parliament and the States may impose restrictions only in accordance with Articles 302 to 305.

examTips: Free trade/commerce/intercourse throughout India; subject to Part XIII restrictions.

keyTakeaways: Art 301: freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse throughout India.
